title: The Tires I Fix
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Using the metaphor of changing a flat tire versus overhauling a transmission, Stuart maps the deliberate limits of his work as an educational writer: he addresses overwhelm, demotivation, and lack of clarity, and nothing else. The piece functions as a comprehensive resource catalog organized by three audience types—overwhelmed teachers, teachers facing student motivation problems, and administrators designing PD. For each audience, Stuart lists his books, courses, mini-courses, and free strategies with brief rationale for each. The article serves both as a practical reference guide and an honest declaration of professional scope, inviting readers to find themselves in one of the three categories and start there. The curated list form makes the piece unusually scannable: a practitioner in any of the three situations can identify their pain point and move directly to the relevant resource.
points: Stuart frames his professional scope as intentionally narrow: he fixes three types of flat tires—overwhelm, demotivation, and lack of clarity—and explicitly disclaims competence in systemic reform, a rare act of professional self-limitation.

For overwhelmed teachers, These 6 Things grants explicit permission to ignore 90% of professional demands and focus deeply on just six high-leverage areas, addressing the common pattern of scattered, exhausting effort across too many fronts.

The MGC strategy (Moments of Genuine Connection) is described as the operating system of a well-functioning classroom—a systematic, clipboard-tracked approach to ensuring every student feels seen, valued, and known, without relying on chance.

Mini-Sermons are presented as an underused tool uniquely in the teacher’s power: no administrator or parent is better positioned to make the case for a subject’s value than the teacher who knows it best.

For administrators, Stuart’s group-viewing mini-course licenses offer a structured faculty PD model—short video followed by facilitated discussion—tested across schools nationwide and priced by viewer count.
quotes: I'm not a mechanic, but I can change a flat tire. I don't know how to fix a transmission or build an engine, but if you're stranded on the side of the road with a popped tire, I got you.

My work as a writer is a lot like that. I can’t figure out how to overhaul the school system to make it better. (I mean, except for four-day schoolweeks… .) But, I can help with a few basic problems: Overwhelm (for teachers, administrators, students); Demotivation (for teachers, admin, students); Clarity.

Moments of Genuine Connection. This is the operating system of a well-functioning classroom. Stop leaving care signals to chance, start peacefully and systematically ensuring that every student knows that you see, value, and know them.

Mini-Sermons. No one is better situated to speak to the Value of the courses I teach than me. Not parents, not administrators, not the culture. I know all the ways in which my subject is good and its work is worthwhile.
Every educator has experienced bad professional development, and that’s because creating enjoyable and productive professional development experiences is hard stuff.

The genius of John Wooden wasn’t in accruing more championship rings than he could fit on one hand; it was in breaking basketball down into its smallest pieces and making these pieces crystal clear for his students.
